does: Makes small holes in a skin or a crust with the tip of a knife or a fork, so that steam can leave and the skin does not split or the crust puff.

intro.what: Pricking makes small shallow holes in a skin or pastry crust.
intro.why: It teaches you to create steam outlets without turning a delicate surface into tears or deep cuts.

how: Dry the surface, so that the tip does not slip.
Prick evenly all over with the point, a little way in, about as far apart as the width of a fork.
On a sausage, turn it and prick on every side. On pastry, prick the base and the sides.
Cook it soon after, before the holes close.

cues.text: A neat spread of small holes all over, none of them a tear.

mistakes.mistake: Stabbing deep into a sausage, which lets the juices run out and dries it.
mistakes.fix: Prick only just through the skin.

mistakes.mistake: Pricking unevenly, which leaves a patch that still splits or puffs.

quiz.question: What do the small holes made by pricking allow?
choices: Steam to escape instead of forcing a surface to puff or split.
The entire filling to drain out freely.
A thick solid crust to become completely sealed.
quiz.because: Small openings release steam that could otherwise lift or split the surface.

quiz.question: How should the holes be distributed?
choices: Only in a dense cluster at an edge.
As deep long slashes through the food.
quiz.because: Even coverage avoids untreated patches where steam can still push the surface upward.

quiz.question: Which appearance fits careful pricking?
choices: Long ragged splits across the surface.
quiz.because: The aim is controlled small openings rather than structural damage.

quiz.question: A pastry patch puffed while the rest stayed flat. What would you change next time?
choices: Prick the surface more evenly, including missed areas.
Make every existing hole much deeper.
Leave more of the base unpricked.
quiz.because: An unpricked patch can still trap steam even when neighbouring areas have outlets.

variant_of.differs: Scoring cuts shallow lines. Pricking makes only small holes and takes nothing away, so that steam leaves without the skin or the crust splitting or puffing.
